statement: In laboratory tests of the first commercial nitazene test strip (BTNX Rapid Response; maker's cut-off 2000 ng/mL isotonitazene) on pure nitazene standards in water and on nearly pure seized powders, compared with known content, the strips detected most nitazenes tested but missed one group entirely. Read from photographs by two blinded raters and by image analysis, isotonitazene read positive in all six replicates from 3000 ng/mL with one lot and 2000 ng/mL with another, obtained about four months apart. With one lot and one strip per concentration, 24 of 33 nitazene analogues read positive at 9000 ng/mL or less; nine did not at 9000 ng/mL: the six desnitazenes, which lack the 5-nitro group (among them metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene), 5-aminoisotonitazene and two analogues with a longer link between the rings. Six seized powders, each estimated as more than 90% one nitazene, all read positive at about 1 and 0.1 mg/mL (6 of 6; editors' Wilson 95% CI 61.0–100%) (De Vrieze et al., 2024). In a second laboratory, the strips detected metonitazene from 1 µg/mL and N-piperidinyl etonitazene and protonitazene from 5 µg/mL (ten strips per level), and reacted to none of 76 other drugs, cutting agents and other compounds at two concentrations (Sisco et al., 2024b). No study read tested nitazene-free street samples or mixtures in which a nitazene is a small part of heroin, other opioids or stimulants, so how often the strips miss nitazenes or give false positives in real samples is unknown; preliminary street-sample figures cited from the maker's material (12 samples) are unpublished. The first study's authors write that a negative result does not mean a sample is free of nitazenes or safe, and that a positive one does not show which nitazene is present or how much. Certainty: very low. Status: replicated.
plain: In laboratory tests, nitazene test strips showed most nitazenes (24 of 33 tested) and all six nearly pure seized powders. They missed one group, the desnitazenes, even in large amounts. Only pure drugs were tested, so how well they work on mixed street drugs is not known.
population: Nitazene reference standards in water (33 analogues in one laboratory, three in another), six nearly pure seized nitazene powders, and 76 other drugs, cutting agents and other compounds
exposure: BTNX Rapid Response nitazene test strips (two lots), read from photographs by two blinded raters and by image analysis, or by laboratory staff
comparator: Known content of prepared solutions; LC-QTOF-MS identification of the main compound in each powder
outcome: Lowest isotonitazene concentration detected, which analogues read positive, readings of the powders, and reactions to other compounds
magnitude: De Vrieze et al.: isotonitazene limit (all six replicates positive) 3000 ng/mL (lot A) and 2000 ng/mL (lot B), the same by visual and image-analysis scoring; analogues (lot B, single strips) 24 of 33 positive at 9000 ng/mL or less (visually 16 at 1000 and 3000 ng/mL, 7 at 3000 ng/mL only, 1 at 9000 ng/mL only), 9 not detected at 9000 ng/mL; powders 6 of 6 positive at both concentrations (Wilson 95% CI 61.0–100%, editors' calculation on the card). Sisco et al. (2024b): limits 1 µg/mL (metonitazene) and 5 µg/mL (N-piperidinyl etonitazene, protonitazene); no reaction with 76 non-nitazene compounds at 0.01 and 0.5 or 1 mg/mL.

evidence.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Limit of detection, 1st paragraph; Results › Limit of detection, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 3rd paragraph
evidence.extracted: Isotonitazene at 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 3000 ng/mL and a blank, each tested on three days in duplicate with two lots (six replicates per concentration and lot); with the limit defined as the lowest concentration at which all replicates read positive, it was 3000 ng/mL for lot A and 2000 ng/mL for lot B, by both visual and ImageJ scoring. The lots were obtained about four months apart.

evidence.extracted: With lot B and one strip per concentration, 24 of 33 nitazene analogues were detectable at or below 9000 ng/mL (visually 16 at both 1000 and 3000 ng/mL, 7 at 3000 ng/mL only, N-piperidinyl etonitazene at 9000 ng/mL only) and 9 were not detectable at 9000 ng/mL: the six desnitazenes lacking the 5-nitro group (compounds 19–24), 5-aminoisotonitazene (26) and the two ethylene-linker analogues (31 and 32); 5-methyl etodesnitazene was the only desnitazene detected. Brorphine at 1 mg/mL did not cross-react (data not shown).

evidence.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Testing of authentic powder samples, 1st paragraph; Results › Testing of authentic powder samples, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: Six seized powders (metonitazene, protonitazene, isotonitazene, butonitazene and two N-pyrrolidino etonitazene samples), each with the nitazene as the major compound at an estimated purity above 90% by LC-QTOF-MS, were each tested once at about 1 mg/mL and once at a tenfold lower concentration, with some powder undissolved: all readings were positive by both scoring methods, and the blank was negative. Editors' calculation on the study card: 6 of 6, Wilson 95% CI 61.0–100%.

evidence.extracted: The maker states that the strips are calibrated with isotonitazene (cut-off 2000 ng/mL), detect three other analogues (listed cut-offs 1300 to 4500 ng/mL), do not detect metodesnitazene or etodesnitazene at 100 µg/mL, and do not cross-react with listed cutting agents and drugs at 100 µg/mL or more. Preliminary third-party figures cited from the maker's material: 24 of 29 analogues cross-reacting at 3000 ng/mL in one screen (including metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene, which this study did not detect), and sensitivity of 100% and 89% at two sample dilutions with specificity of 100% in 12 street samples; unpublished and not read.

evidence.extracted: The authors did not repeat the maker's specificity tests apart from brorphine and call for studies of street samples to look for false positives and for false negatives caused by interfering compounds; they conclude that a negative result does not mean a sample is safe, since it may contain non-reacting nitazenes, other synthetic opioids, other drugs or adulterants, and that a positive result gives no information on the identity, quantity or purity of the nitazene present.

evidence.locator: Results and Discussion › Limit of Detection, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs (AM p. 6); Cross-Reactivity, 2nd and 6th paragraphs (AM pp. 7–8); Table 1 (AM p. 16); Table 3 (AM p. 19)
evidence.extracted: BTNX nitazene strips in water (positive control metonitazene, listed cut-off 2 µg/mL): approximate limit of detection 1 µg/mL for metonitazene and 5 µg/mL for N-piperidinyl etonitazene and protonitazene. In the cross-reactivity panel of 79 analytes, tested with two strips each at 0.5 or 1 mg/mL and at 0.01 mg/mL, the strips reacted to the three nitazenes and to nothing else, with no faint results (Table 3). Editors' count: 76 non-nitazene compounds gave clear negatives.
evidence.source_read: PDF PDFs/Cannabis/Sisco_2023_XylazineTestStrips.pdf (NIST author manuscript of Sisco et al., 2024b, despite the file name; AM p. = PDF page)

risk_of_bias.note: QUADAS-2 high for De Vrieze et al. (study card: pure positives and blank negatives, a two-gate design that can overstate accuracy, though raters were blinded and replicated); Sisco et al. (2024b) has no instrument and is filed in-vitro.

inconsistency.note: The two laboratories' detection limits are of the same order (1 to 5 µg/mL); four compounds differ from an unpublished third-party screen, which is second-hand and not counted.

indirectness.note: Pure standards and nearly pure powders in water, trained raters, one brand and two lots; the claim is about strips used on real samples.

imprecision.note: Analogue results rest on one strip per concentration; six powders give a lower 95% bound of 61%; specificity was tested only in pure solutions.

publication_bias.note: Not assessable from these sources; laboratory evaluations of test strips are not registered.

grade.reasoning: Test-accuracy evidence starts high; one level each for risk of bias, indirectness and imprecision gives very low. Rated as worded: laboratory detection of nitazenes by one brand of strip. Status replicated: two independent laboratories (Ghent University; NIST) found detection at µg/mL concentrations. The preliminary street-sample figures are second-hand from the maker's material and not counted.
